changelog: v3.9.0.0: Encode priority, off by default: the plugin writes a list of what capped viewers are watching into each encoder's source folder so those copies are made first. New per-policy "Play within-cap versions as they are", off by default: a version within the cap is not transcoded when a client's bitrate limit is the only reason. The copy suffix list no longer gains another " - 720p" on every restart. v3.8.2.0: A library with one folder per season at its root gets one Series item per folder, and the once-per-show intro rule was keyed on that per-folder SeriesId, so the intro returned with every new season. The cache and the play-history check now key on the show presentation key, with SeriesId as the fallback. v3.8.1.0: The intro played again on every episode after a server restart. The once-per-series rule read LastPlayedDate on the Series item, which Jellyfin never writes, so only an in-memory cache held the intro back and every restart cleared it. The check now asks the library for a played or resumable episode under the series, which holds across seasons and restarts. v3.8.0.0: A request made with a Jellyfin API key, or with no credentials, carries no user id, so it matched no policy and was served uncapped on every route. A new setting names the policy such requests are held to. Unset by default, so upgrading changes nothing.
description: Quality Gate lets Jellyfin administrators cap the resolution a user may be served. The cap is measured against the media's actual height, read from its video stream, so it holds whatever the file is called. Media above the cap is served as a capped transcode, or as a lower-resolution version of the same item where one exists, and requests for the original file are refused. Useful for bandwidth management and tiered access.
name: QualityGate
overview: Cap the resolution a user may be served, measured against the media's actual height.
